session_4.result:
I added `dedupe` and `copy ID`, and all 20 tests pass. The commit is `1dc7721`. I left the `.pyc` deletions that were already in your working tree out of it.

- **`dedupe`:** It archives duplicates instead of deleting them, following the no-hard-delete rule. Among active tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at` and archives the rest. If two have the same `due_at`, it keeps the lower id. Tasks that are already archived are ignored. It prints how many it archived.
- **`copy ID`:** It creates a task titled `<original title> (copy)` with exactly the same `due_at` as the original. It passes the title through `normalize_title()` in the CLI. I added a `copy_task` function in `api.py` rather than reusing `create_task`, because `create_task` works from "seconds from now" and would give a slightly different `due_at`. If the id doesn't exist, it prints "no such task".

Normalizing the whole title truncates at 80 characters. A very long original title will lose its " (copy)" suffix.

I didn't touch `delete_task` or the `delete` command. The new tests cover both commands through the API and the CLI.
